nodes.label: fuser (FUSE for Rust)
nodes.author: Christopher Berner
nodes.rationale: A rewrite of the FUSE C library rather than bindings, replacing libfuse between the kernel driver and the userspace implementation so a developer gets Rust's type interface and runtime; on Linux the mount/umount libfuse calls are optional and removable via the libfuse feature flag. Forked from the zargony fuse crate to continue development past ABI 7.19.

nodes.label: Local Quality Gate (scripts/check.sh)
nodes.rationale: Runs cargo fmt --check, clippy with -D warnings across all targets/features, the workspace test suite, and cargo doc. On a Mac without the macFUSE SDK it uses fuser's compile-only macos-no-mount mode so the callback and binary API still receive static analysis.

nodes.label: macfuse Feature Gate
nodes.rationale: Native macFUSE mounting is kept behind a cargo feature so ordinary workspace builds and tests do not require an installed macFUSE 4 SDK or system extension.

nodes.label: Rust 1.88 / Edition 2024 Prerequisite
nodes.rationale: Rust 1.85 first stabilized edition 2024, but the dependency graph raises the supported minimum to 1.88; distribution Cargo packages are frequently too old, so rustup-managed stable is required for rust-toolchain.toml to be honored.

nodes.label: fuser macos-no-mount Compile-Only Mode
nodes.rationale: Lets a Mac without the macFUSE SDK still type-check the full callback and binary API, which is exactly what quicKFS's check.sh relies on for Clippy coverage.

nodes.label: fuser CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Ubuntu jobs build/test with and without the libfuse feature plus a musl target, cargo-deny runs pinned at 0.16.2, and the macos-26 job checks the macos-no-mount compile-only path before full builds because hosted macOS runners cannot mount macFUSE.

nodes.label: fuser Changelog
nodes.rationale: 0.17.0 moved Filesystem trait methods to &self requiring Send + Sync + 'static, replaced Vec<MountOption> with a structured Config API, added multi-threaded event loops (Config::n_threads) and an experimental AsyncFilesystem, and made abi-7-xx feature flags runtime checks instead of compile-time gates.

nodes.label: Platform Ports Excluded From This Backlog
nodes.norm_label: platform ports excluded from this backlog

nodes.label: Server-Pushed Cross-Client Cache Invalidation (planned)
nodes.rationale: Local post-mutation projections are already invalidated coherently; the blocker is that synchronous fuser notifications from inside macOS callbacks are unsafe with the single receive loop.

nodes.label: quicKFS Roadmap Priorities
nodes.rationale: Ordered: recovery/live-session revocation/per-user export roots/audit logging/independent review; fault-injection and Linux+macOS CI; server-pushed cross-client cache invalidation and observability; signed overlapping pin rotation, keychain, packaging; WinFsp support. Cold-start offline mounting and offline writes are intentionally deferred pending authenticated durable journals, version preconditions, revalidation, conflict policy, and reconciliation.

nodes.label: Windows Server (not planned)
nodes.rationale: Not implemented or currently planned for the initial milestones.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Offline Writes
nodes.rationale: Mutating while disconnected would create merge risk: two clients editing overlapping ranges, racing renames/deletes, pathname reuse, or both believing they hold an exclusive lock, while the server may revoke access, change quota, or start a new export epoch. A safe design needs a durable idempotent mutation journal, base revisions and preconditions, stable object identity, reauthentication with permission/quota/lock revalidation, defined conflict rules, and user-visible reconciliation. Until then writes fail closed. This is deliberately an SMB-like read/page cache, not a synchronization product.

nodes.label: No Cold-Start Offline Mount
nodes.rationale: Without contacting the server a client cannot authenticate the current server identity and account, confirm the export epoch, learn that permissions were not revoked, or prove its cached namespace is current. Serving cached data only after a previously authenticated online mount disconnects keeps stale entries from becoming an unauthenticated substitute filesystem.

nodes.label: quickfs-client-cli
nodes.rationale: The old --cert and shared --token options were removed; without a CA option an exact pin from pairing or managed import is required, and --trust-system-roots/--ca-cert are mutually exclusive and apply only to authenticated commands, not pair/forget/trust import.

nodes.label: quickfs-server-daemon serve
nodes.rationale: Every resource is explicitly bounded: read/write sizes, open handles, per-connection and global known nodes, directory-entry worker tasks, request timeout, request concurrency, in-flight read/write byte budgets, connection count, Argon2 workers, and per-source auth attempts.

nodes.label: Linux Server Deployment
nodes.rationale: Linux is the deployment target. The state directory holds the secret identity, password hashes, and pairing records and must be a disjoint tree from the export root, with 0700 directories and 0600 files. A systemd unit is planned, not supplied.

nodes.label: macOS Server (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: Not implemented; the initial server target is Linux. The daemon still runs on macOS for development without Linux-only special-node creation.

nodes.label: Two-Gate Write Authorization
nodes.rationale: A mutation requires both the export-wide daemon --allow-writes gate and the account's own write grant, so read-only is the default at two independent levels and the volume mounts read-only unless both allow it.

nodes.label: Lossless Unix Byte Names
nodes.rationale: macOS lookup tries exact bytes first, then NFD/case-insensitive folding only when both names are valid UTF-8; ambiguous folded names fail rather than selecting the wrong file. macOS rejects invalid UTF-8 pathnames before they reach the adapter, so only Linux and the wire format preserve them.

nodes.label: Metadata Wire Record
nodes.rationale: Field order is wire order and must not change. There is deliberately no distinct ctime field: adding one is a positional struct change Postcard cannot carry compatibly within a major.

nodes.label: Known Non-Additive Changes
nodes.rationale: Distinct ctime on Metadata (a positional field on a struct embedded in ~a dozen responses) and server-initiated push (a transport-shaped change, not an enum append) are deferred precisely because they cannot be compatible minors.

nodes.label: Guideline: Adding a Protocol Version
nodes.rationale: Add never reshape: append new enum variants at the end, never insert/reorder/remove; never change an existing struct's field count, order, or type; gate emission on negotiation with a MINOR_<FEATURE> floor and predicate; self-describing frame flags may be decoded unconditionally but setting them is still negotiated; bump PROTOCOL_MINOR and record it; prove all four old/new client x server combinations in tests. A change that cannot obey these is a major bump, which changes the ALPN and is a genuine flag day. There is no intermediate 'breaking but same-ALPN' tier until a per-major capability bitset lands.

nodes.label: Postcard Positional Serialization
nodes.rationale: Postcard is compact but non-self-describing: struct fields are positional with no names or count and enum variants are identified by declaration-order index. There is no tolerance for a missing or extra trailing field and #[serde(default)] does not rescue a shortened struct on the wire, which is exactly why every compatibility rule below exists.

nodes.label: fuser FreeBSD Cirrus CI Task
nodes.rationale: Runs on freebsd-14-3 with fusefs kldloaded, builds a pinned pjdfstest revision from source, and runs the BSD mount test plus the pjdfs conformance suite.

nodes.label: macfuse-ci Composite Action
nodes.rationale: Shared macFUSE CI steps (Homebrew PATH resolution for both /opt/homebrew and /usr/local, stable Rust, libfuse-feature tests, the macos-mount test, and the macOS pjdfs suite) factored out so the PR and push workflows stay identical.

nodes.label: MacStadium PR CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Real macFUSE mount testing needs a self-hosted MacStadium runner; the PR variant is bound to the macstadium environment as an approval gate so an untrusted pull request cannot execute on the self-hosted host without review.

nodes.label: MacStadium Push CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the same composite action on pushes to master without the environment approval gate, since the code is already trusted at that point.

nodes.label: Cache Writer Backpressure
nodes.rationale: Opportunistic read-through stores are dropped past 1,024 queued jobs or 128 MiB of queued range payloads (the in-memory tiers still serve them) so queue latency and memory stay bounded; coherence-critical invalidations and waited inserts are never dropped.

nodes.label: Cheap Content-Addressed Stores
nodes.rationale: Payload hashing and the atomic payload write happen before the state lock (file names are content-addressed, so this is concurrency-safe), and a store whose manifest entry is already current skips the clone and commit entirely.

nodes.label: Process-Local Hot Range Tier
nodes.rationale: A bounded 256 MiB tier keeps a cold persistent block in memory after one integrity check so later small FUSE reads slice it locally instead of rereading and rehashing the whole block.

nodes.label: Bounded Persistent Read-Through Cache
nodes.rationale: Keyed by node plus exact file revision; namespaces bind the authenticated certificate fingerprint, persisted server epoch, and username so cached data can never cross an identity or authorization boundary. Payloads are SHA-256 checked, atomically written, owner-private, and LRU-evicted under a hard byte budget.

nodes.label: Epoch-Matched Authenticated Reconnect
nodes.rationale: Reconnect accepts only the same persisted server epoch. Revision-matched handles are reopened and live-client lock state replayed after a daemon restart; locks are not immortal disk state, so closing or disconnecting the owner releases them.

nodes.label: macFUSE Installation Preflight
nodes.rationale: Every macOS client process checks for the macFUSE bundle at startup and exits with the installation link; quicKFS deliberately does not install, approve, or update the system extension. The check is repeated per launch so there is no cached result to clear.

nodes.label: quickfs-mount (macOS)
nodes.rationale: Built separately because it links the macFUSE 4 SDK. It verifies the trust policy before the password prompt, reconnects under the same policy, and keeps one shared Tokio runtime around an authenticated reconnecting RemoteFilesystem plus the persistent cache. Cached reads survive a disconnect but write opens and mutations fail closed and a mount cannot cold-start offline.

nodes.label: Adaptive Sequential Read-Ahead
nodes.rationale: macFUSE issues sequential access as independent read callbacks, so only one range request is ever in flight and a high-latency link sits idle. A speculative window scheduled ahead of the consumer, sharing the revision-keyed single-flight gate with demand reads, keeps the pipe full; a mutation bumps the file revision and orphans speculative blocks so read-after-write coherence holds.

nodes.label: Buffer Depth Is Not Fetch Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Fetching a whole window at once runs the link as a convoy: QUIC fair-shares bandwidth so each block completes in in-flight-bytes/link-rate and a demand miss waits that long (64 x 1 MiB in flight gave 1-3.5 s fetches and frozen playback). Speculation is bounded by a 32 MiB global in-flight byte pool (64 KiB units), a global cap of 8 concurrent speculative fetches, and a per-read burst of 8 blocks. The byte pool is the convoy ceiling, deliberately decoupled from --read-ahead-max-bytes, because with 8 MiB blocks the 8-fetch cap alone would put 64 MiB on the wire (playback demand spiked to ~700 ms; capping at 32 MiB dropped it to ~130 ms). Budgets use non-blocking try_acquire so an unaffordable block is unscheduled rather than parked, since a parked fetch counts as in-flight and leaves a never-fetched hole. Each speculative fetch carries a 120 s deadline; demand reads never take permits.
nodes.norm_label: buffer depth is not fetch concurrency

nodes.label: Cold-Start Read-Ahead Priming
nodes.rationale: Arming the window only after two in-order reads, at one block, left a freshly opened file with a serial cold ramp that stalled paced playback 150 ms-1 s (≈1 s under a concurrent Finder crawl). The first read of a handle now primes shallow speculation and a confirmed run arms several blocks deep; priming is gated on there being no tracked stream so mid-file seeks and thumbnail crawls do not waste read-ahead. Measured stalls drop to zero with per-read latency under ~75 ms.

nodes.label: Persistent Write-Behind Group Commit
nodes.rationale: Rewriting the whole manifest per mutation is O(total entries) under the state mutex every lookup needs; with tens of thousands of entries a read-ahead plus thumbnail burst floods the single writer thread with hours of backlog and the filesystem appears hung while the network is idle. The writer now drains batches of 256 jobs and writes the manifest once per batch, removing obsolete payloads only after that write to preserve manifest-first crash ordering; enqueue_and_wait still completes only after its batch flush so completion implies durability.

nodes.label: Multiple Sequential Streams Per Handle
nodes.rationale: macOS multiplexes independent readers (player page-ins, Spotlight, Quick Look) over one FUSE fh. Tracking up to four streams per handle with LRU slot recycling stops one reader's seeks from destroying another's window; the earlier single-stream design zeroed the window dozens of times per minute during video playback.

nodes.label: macOS Kernel Read-Ahead Disabled (-o noreadahead)
nodes.rationale: The macOS kernel's speculative read machinery is tuned for microsecond-latency local disks and is harmful on a network filesystem: it raced 100+ MB ahead of a paced consumer in 16 KiB page-ins, had those pages evicted, and re-read the same regions in multi-hundred-megabyte sweeps (5.5x read amplification) while the player's page-in queued 2-4 s behind. Disabling it volume-wide and delegating pipelining to the client prefetcher gave zero stalls in 60 s paced playback and roughly doubled cold sequential throughput (26.8 -> 49.8 MB/s). The page cache and mmap remain enabled.

nodes.label: Stall-Driven Window Sizing
nodes.rationale: The window doubles only when a demand read actually blocked >=10 ms on the network (direct evidence the window is under the bandwidth-delay product), at most once per half-window of delivered bytes, and holds while reads are prefetch hits. An earlier throughput hill-climber whipsawed between one and four blocks because throughput measured over demand-blocked time is pure noise once reads become cache hits. Bounded by --read-ahead-max-bytes (64 MiB default).

nodes.label: Best-Effort Unmount With Watchdog
nodes.rationale: Unmount performs no synchronous network cleanup so it never depends on a live server: handle closes are best-effort under a short bound, Control+C falls back to a forced local macFUSE detach after three seconds, and a process-level eight-second watchdog bounds even a wedged OS unmount call.

nodes.label: Aligned Read-Through Fill Sizing
nodes.rationale: Sequential/copy-sized reads align to the configured block up to the 16 MiB range limit, while sub-1 MiB probes use at most a 1 MiB aligned fill so Finder metadata/thumbnail inspection does not pull 16 MiB from every touched file. Server-side copy carries no raw body so the server can use reflink/copy-range acceleration without round-tripping bytes.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Mutation Non-Retry Rule
nodes.rationale: A mutation's outcome after a transport failure may already have taken effect, so it is never blindly retried (AmbiguousMutation, mapped to EIO). Safe reads and lookups may reconnect and retry; a handle is reopened only when the persistent epoch and exact file revision still match.

nodes.label: End-to-End Callback Timeout Budget
nodes.rationale: --callback-timeout-ms is one 120 s absolute budget covering the initial request, connection replacement, reconnect backoff, reauthentication, handle reopening/lock replay, and a safe retry; no phase restarts it, and the callback bridge adds only a fixed 100 ms margin to deliver the typed result. A stalled connection generation is marked unhealthy so later demand does not reselect it, and a shared reconnect outlives the waiter that started it because it remains useful to others. Idempotent exhaustion maps to ETIMEDOUT; an ambiguous mutation maps to EIO and is never retried.

nodes.label: Node-Wide Directory Snapshot Invalidation
nodes.rationale: An enriched directory snapshot embeds each child's metadata, so any content/attribute/xattr/link/rename/exchange/remove must invalidate every cached snapshot containing that node, committed in one manifest transaction. Metadata is retained for the same 30-second lifetime as the snapshot so a second callback wave cannot degrade into one GetMetadata per child.

nodes.label: Enriched Revision-Validated Directory Projection
nodes.rationale: One request replaces a per-callback RPC storm: current/parent metadata, every child with metadata, complete xattr names, and bounded small xattr values. The adapter single-flights cold loads, creates stable local inodes, and answers the resulting lookup/getattr/listxattr/negative-xattr burst locally; directory and embedded-child metadata share one 30-second lifetime so children cannot expire mid-wave.

nodes.label: Server Node Registry
nodes.rationale: Maps each opaque node UUID to its backing device+inode and known paths. Global entries whose refcount reaches zero are retained as a least-recently-found cache so reconnect keeps stable node IDs, and evicted lazily only under pressure. Each tracked node costs roughly 400-500 bytes.

nodes.label: ErrorCode Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Codes map to the platform adapter's native errno (NotFound->ENOENT, TooLarge->EFBIG, Conflict/InvalidNode->ESTALE); UnsupportedVersion is returned uncompressed when a peer's major differs from 6.

nodes.label: Raw I/O Bodies
nodes.rationale: ReadRange/GetXattr responses and WriteRange/SetXattr requests state a byte count then send exactly that many raw bytes on the same stream, never compressed at this layer because file bytes are typically already-compressed media.

nodes.label: Slow Directory Listing Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: A fast first ls followed by a ~30 s stall on an immediate second ls identifies the old mismatched child-metadata TTL, which caused a per-child GetMetadata wave that outlived the directory view. Raising --callback-timeout-ms only hides symptoms; --max-directory-entry-tasks (default 64) can hurt a saturated rotational array.

nodes.label: Directory Opens Without FOPEN_CACHE_DIR
nodes.rationale: The adapter's coherent snapshot already covers Finder's follow-up callbacks, while an extra kernel directory pin could hide a completed mutation. Synchronous fuser invalidation notifications are also never issued from inside a callback because the single macOS receive loop can block on them.

nodes.label: Frame Compression (minor 6.3)
nodes.rationale: Negotiated then opportunistic: a frame is compressed only when the partner advertises >= 6.3, the payload is >= 1 KiB, and the compressed form is actually smaller, so tiny or incompressible bodies are never enlarged. zstd level 3 is the throughput/ratio sweet spot. Enriched directory views are the target, compressing roughly 7x on a realistic media library, which directly speeds cold WAN crawls. Compression happens after Postcard encoding and after chunk packing so the frame limit and paging are measured uncompressed; decompression output is bounded to MAX_FRAME_SIZE as a decompression-bomb guard.

nodes.label: Per-Connection and Global Known-Node Limits
nodes.rationale: Semaphore counters bounding the live working set, not the export size; their purpose is memory/DoS protection against a client that looks up nodes without ever forgetting them. Defaults were raised to 131072/524288 because macOS keeps a 100k-300k vnode cache and auto_xattr AppleDouble sidecars roughly double the working set during a crawl, so the old 8192/65536 were undersized.

nodes.label: Metadata Batching (minor 6.4)
nodes.rationale: A cold crawl otherwise pays a full RTT per GetMetadata, which dominates WAN latency even with readdirplus-style enrichment. GetMetadataBatch resolves up to 4096 nodes per round trip with positional results in request order; a per-node failure is reported in place as BatchedMetadata::Failed so one unresolved node never discards the rest. The 4096 cap keeps the reply inside one 1 MiB frame (no streaming path) and bounds server fan-out; an over-limit batch is rejected whole with TooLarge rather than truncated. The client emits it only when the server advertises >= 6.4 and otherwise falls back to per-node GetMetadata; the server needs no version check because it only receives.

nodes.label: Self-Healing Node Eviction
nodes.rationale: Neither ceiling is a hard wall. A full global pool evicts a globally-unreferenced cached entry and retries; an exhausted per-connection working set evicts one of its own nodes (skipping the root and any node backing an open handle) and retries. macOS reclaims vnodes lazily, so without this a long-lived mount would eventually fail every getattr/lookup of a new node with 'too many known nodes' (ErrorCode::TooLarge, surfaced as EFBIG) until remounted. Evicting only drops that connection's reference; the node stays in the larger global registry with an unchanged stable identifier, so nothing cached goes stale.

nodes.label: peer_supports_<feature> Capability Gating
nodes.rationale: A peer emits an optional feature only when the partner advertises support at or above the feature's floor minor, so a newer peer withholds what an older same-major peer cannot parse and no flag day is needed.

nodes.label: Major.Minor Version Negotiation
nodes.rationale: The version word packs major in the high byte and minor in the low byte of a u16. The ALPN is keyed to the major only (quickfs/6) so every 6.x peer still connects instead of failing at the TLS handshake; per-request checks accept any same-major minor and hard-reject only a different major. Each peer learns the other's exact version (client from HelloAck, server from every request envelope) so the server holds no per-connection version state.

nodes.label: Streamed Directory-View Pagination (minor 6.1)
nodes.rationale: A projection larger than one 1 MiB frame streams as DirectoryViewStart / Chunk(s) / End from one revision-consistent server snapshot, so there is no cursor to expire and no cross-page skew; the client reassembles an identical DirectoryView so callers above the transport see one result either way. An entry too large for one chunk sheds its inline xattr values (still reachable via GetXattr). Both peers cap the materialized set at MAX_DIRECTORY_ENTRIES (1,048,576) as a memory backstop.

nodes.label: Argon2id Password Storage
nodes.rationale: Salted PHC-format Argon2id hashes are verified in a globally bounded blocking worker pool so memory-hard hashing cannot block or exhaust the async network runtime.

nodes.label: Login and Pairing Rate Limits
nodes.rationale: Five failures per connection, 30 attempts per source IP per rolling minute, and at most four global Argon2 jobs. Pairing shares the same per-source limiter so an unauthenticated peer cannot probe pairing records faster than passwords. Distributed guessing and account lockout remain out of scope.

nodes.label: Length-Prefixed Frame Layout
nodes.rationale: A 4-byte big-endian prefix whose high bit is FRAME_COMPRESSED_FLAG and whose low 31 bits are the body length. Because a real length never reaches bit 31 (MAX_FRAME_SIZE is 1 MiB) the flag can never collide with a length, and a receiver must reject an over-large declared length before allocating.

nodes.label: quicKFS Wire Protocol Specification v6.4
nodes.rationale: Normative for a second implementation or an audit; crates/protocol/src/lib.rs is the canonical source of truth and wins any disagreement.

nodes.label: Pairing and Login Setup Flow
nodes.rationale: Pairing and login are deliberately separate: pairing sends no username or password and does not log in, and login authorizes filesystem operations for one QUIC connection only. Trust records are keyed by both --server and --server-name, so both must match between pairing and later use.

nodes.label: quicKFS Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Clients and the network are untrusted; the server host, export owner, identity state, account administration, pairing-secret distribution, managed pin channel, and configured roots are trusted. A compromised server private key permits impersonation wherever the client's trust policy accepts its certificate. Traffic analysis, compromised endpoints, production recovery/live-session revocation, per-user export isolation, formal protocol analysis, and large distributed availability attacks are out of scope for the prototype.

nodes.label: Pairing-Assisted TOFU
nodes.rationale: An out-of-band 160-bit one-time secret authenticates the first trust decision, so this is not plain TOFU. Domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 proofs bind pairing ID, presented certificate fingerprint, and a fresh nonce in both directions, so a wrong code never consumes the record and a MITM presenting a different certificate cannot relay a matching proof. High-entropy text codes were chosen over short numeric codes to avoid offline guessing without shipping an unaudited PAKE.

nodes.label: Server Trust Separated From User Login
nodes.rationale: Establishing server trust does not log a user in; a password is never sent until the selected trust policy has authenticated the server certificate, so a MITM never receives a credential.
nodes.norm_label: server trust separated from user login

nodes.label: Trust-Policy TLS Preflight
nodes.rationale: Because an interactive password prompt can outlast a QUIC idle timeout, the CLI validates trust on a preflight connection, closes it, prompts, then opens a fresh connection and applies the same in-memory policy again before transmitting the credential.

nodes.label: Crate Change Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Wire types in crates/protocol (docs/protocol.md updated with every protocol change), quinn/rustls in crates/transport-quic, filesystem policy and export-root confinement in crates/server-core, platform-independent client behavior in crates/client-core, macOS bindings under clients/macos. thiserror in libraries, anyhow only at binary entry points, and #![forbid(unsafe_code)] preserved unless a platform binding makes narrowly isolated unsafe unavoidable.

nodes.label: Export-Root Confinement
nodes.rationale: Absolute symlink targets and targets containing .. are rejected to preserve confinement. Xattrs on the symlink object itself are rejected because portable descriptor-relative Unix APIs cannot address them without a path race.

nodes.label: Client Trust Database
nodes.rationale: Pins are keyed by server address plus server name; the client rejects symlinked, wrongly owned, or overly permissive trust state.

nodes.label: Enterprise Private CA Trust Mode
nodes.rationale: A deployed CA bundle plus --server-name validation lets leaf certificates rotate without client re-pairing; CA modes deliberately never fall back to a pin or pairing when validation fails.

nodes.label: identity install Generation Rotation
nodes.rationale: Validated renewals are written as new private generations selected atomically via active-identity; old generations remain protected for administrative recovery.

nodes.label: Managed Exact Certificate Pin
nodes.rationale: MDM distributes the expected leaf SHA-256 fingerprint so unmanaged per-user administrator contact is unnecessary; import refuses silent replacement so an unexpected key change can never become trusted automatically.

nodes.label: Server Identity State Directory
nodes.rationale: Mode 0700 directories / 0600 files; the daemon rejects symlinked, non-regular, wrongly owned, or group/other-accessible state and refuses to start when state and export directories overlap in either direction, which would expose the private key, password database, and pairing records to authenticated filesystem clients.

nodes.label: Enterprise Setup Without Per-Client Pairing
nodes.rationale: QuickFS parses the chain and verifies leaf/key match and QUIC/TLS usability, but clients remain the authority for lifetime, name, and CA-chain validation. The staging key stays outside QuickFS state and must be retired by the organization's secret-delivery policy.

nodes.label: Pinned Server Identity Changed
nodes.rationale: An unexpected identity can mean MITM, wrong address, lost server state, or deliberate replacement. There is no automatic insecure override: the operator must explicitly forget and re-pair or import a managed replacement pin.

nodes.label: Create-Once Administration Lock Files
nodes.rationale: User administration, identity installation, and client trust updates use create-once lock files so concurrent writers cannot lose each other's changes; a killed process can leave .users.lock, .identity.lock, or .trusted-servers.lock behind and only a verified-stale lock may be removed.

nodes.label: Capability-Gated Optional Callbacks
nodes.rationale: copy_file_range, readdirplus, and exchangedata are implemented but gated because the macFUSE 5.3 kernel backend on macOS 15.1 advertises none of them; macFUSE dropped exchangedata on macOS 11 and FSKit requires macOS 15.4+. The protocol/client/server operations remain usable and transport-tested for a future bridge that advertises them.

nodes.label: Split of Server, Client, and Export State
nodes.rationale: Server state (TLS key, Argon2id hashes, pairing records) must never be copied to clients; the export root must stay disjoint from it so authenticated filesystem clients cannot reach secrets.
nodes.norm_label: split of server, client, and export state

hyperedges.label: Server Trust and User Authentication Flow
